character_facts: Aghora is a combatant capable of fighting multiple armored enemies at once.
Aghora is tactical enough to abandon a straightforward fight when it becomes unwinnable.
Aghora is willing to sacrifice part of her resources or weapon to survive.
Aghora can mentally control the metablade strongly enough to trigger and direct its self-destruction.
continuity_links: This page depicts a continuing battle involving Aghora and numerous armored enemies.
The narration frames Aghora’s action as a response to being unable to triumph over all remaining foes.
dialogue_meaning: The captions explain that Aghora changes tactics after realizing total victory over all opponents is impossible.
A warrior code is invoked: survival can demand personal sacrifice.
Aghora mentally turns the metablade’s destructive drive inward, causing it to self-destruct.
She then exploits the resulting explosion as a means of movement or escape through the melee.
locations: A blood-soaked battlefield or combat arena crowded with armored bodies
lore_facts: There is a named rule or maxim associated with Bushitaka that frames survival as requiring self-sacrifice.
The metablade is described as having a violent drive or 'battle-thirst' that can be mentally directed.
The metablade can disintegrate when its destructive force is turned against itself.
Aghora can mentally steer or command the metablade’s destructive energy.
plot_events: Aghora is shown in close combat surrounded by multiple fallen or attacking armored foes.
The narration states that Aghora realizes she cannot overcome every enemy by ordinary means.
She invokes a warrior principle that survival may require sacrificing part of oneself.
Aghora redirects the metablade’s battle-hunger against itself.
Aghora uses the weapon’s self-destructive force as propulsion, blasting away from the crowd of enemies.
uncertainties: Some caption text is small and may not be perfectly legible; wording of the warrior law/maxim may be approximate.
The exact spelling of the lawgiver’s name appears to be 'Bushitaka,' but the lettering is difficult to confirm from the image alone.
The final blast seems to propel Aghora upward or away, but the precise direction is not fully explicit visually.
visual_summary: Aghora fights amid a heap of armored enemies and blood. The narration explains that she cannot defeat all of them directly, so she applies a warrior’s rule of self-sacrifice. She turns the metablade’s violence back onto itself; the weapon begins breaking apart, erupts with force, and Aghora uses that destructive blast to launch herself upward or forward through the battlefield while enemies are thrown below her.
